question: Is the Commission aware of the communication submitted on 7 April 2026 by a group of 60 Romanian NGOs requesting the opening of an EU Pilot procedure concerning Law L143/20261 in Romania, adopted in the context of the implementation of the EU Critical Raw Materials Act, which they allege may introduce provisions granting private mining operators pre-emption rights over private property, establish expedited expropriation mechanisms for commercial mining projects, restrict judicial review, and allow the removal of forest land from Romania’s national forestry fund?
Law L143/2026 is being processed under an emergency procedure, with a tacit adoption deadline set for 22 April 2026.

Given the concerns of the NGOs, does the Commission intend to initiate an EU Pilot or any other preliminary assessment regarding the compatibility of Law L143/2026 with EU law, including the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union, EU environmental legislation, and property rights protections?

In the event that the law is adopted and subsequently found to be incompatible with EU law, what measures does the Commission envisage taking, including but not limited to infringement proceedings under Article 258 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.6.2026) The Commission is aware of and is carefully addressing the communication submitted on 7 April 2026 by a group of 60 Romanian non-governmental organisations requesting the opening of an EU Pilot procedure concerning Law L143/20261 in Romania, as referenced by the Honourable Member. The Commission is currently assessing this communication in detail.

Following this assessment, the Commission will inform the authors of the communication about the most appropriate next steps to address their concerns effectively. These steps could include engaging in a pre-infringement dialogue with the Romanian authorities (formerly referred to as the EU Pilot dialogue)2.

It should also be recalled that national authorities bear the primary responsibility for ensuring the correct application of EU law as well as respecting, in this context, the rights guaranteed under the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union, including by providing effective redress.
